own_solution.law: Archimedes' principle gives equilibrium draught d0 = rho_b L/rho_l. For downward displacement x, the additional upward buoyancy is rho_l g A x. Thus rho_b A L x'' = -rho_l g A x, giving T = 2 pi sqrt(rho_b L/(rho_l g)). With L = 0.30 m, T = 0.886307 s. An attached extension q of the same density and cross-section replaces L by L + q.
assumptions: The cylinder maintains its stated upright orientation and moves vertically.
The displacement is small enough that the cylinder remains partly submerged.
The wood and its attached extension are rigid and have the stated uniform density.
Drag and liquid motion are neglected as instructed.
Lengths are converted from centimetres to metres when using the stated SI gravitational acceleration.
Extensions specified for an earlier run only are absent during the present run.
